payload.feature:
CODEX ENABLEMENT — issue #226 task 11.1, and only what needs no human ruling. Branch slice-codex-enable at HEAD 85cf6d55.

ADOPT YOUR PREDECESSOR'S ITEM 1. Run codex-enablement-issue-226-task--c929d7ec discharged 10.1's three deferred obligations with one exact citation each, and the controller committed that as 85cf6d55. Do not redo it. It then hard-stopped at IMPL-BLOCKED because its Bash grant never reached the session — every cargo call and git write came back 'This command requires approval' while reads were honoured. That was the crew's construction, not the work: its delivery seats were flash offices re-pointed at Claude, carrying the flash lane's tool declaration. You are seated on the NATIVE Claude offices with tools.allow ['cargo','git']. If a build command is still refused, say so immediately as a blocker rather than working around it — do not attempt to verify by reading code alone.

BOTH OF 11.1's STATED DEPENDENCIES ARE NOW DISCHARGED, and the evidence is on this branch. Read it first, in full, before anything else:

  .forge/tasks/controller-codex-proof-2026-09-16-live.json    — the live enforcement, root, accounting and rejection proof (task 10.5, already ticked on main)
  .forge/tasks/controller-codex-interface-2026-09-17.json     — the three obligations 10.1 deferred, measured on the installed binary
  .forge/tools/codex-enforcement-probe.py                     — the instrument that produced the first

Do not re-measure the provider. A boxed seat has no network to reach it; these are controller measurements, taken by hand, and they are the evidence you cite.

WHAT 10.5 ESTABLISHED, on the installed `codex-cli 0.154.0`, every claim attributable to a command that demonstrably ran:
  - A thread opened `-s read-only` denied a write cold, then executed the same write successfully on a BARE resume (exit 0, file present). Decision 0030 ruling 2 holds on this version.
  - Restoring the class denies it again: `cannot create …: Read-only file system`, EXIT=2.
  - `codex exec resume` has NO sandbox flag — `-s` is rejected as an unexpected argument — so `-c sandbox_mode=<class>` is the only channel.
  - Same-root confirmation: the resumed thread id equals the cold one.
  - Accounting is per invocation, not cumulative: two resumes of one thread reported 303 then 308 output tokens.
  - An unknown session id is refused before any turn starts: exit 1, no `thread.started`, no `turn.started`.

WHAT 10.1's DEFERRED OBLIGATIONS NOW HAVE, measured 2026-09-17 on the same binary:
  - **Stdin prompt positional**: the resume subcommand documents `[PROMPT]` as "If `-` is used, read from stdin".
  - **Effort configuration**: `model_reasoning_effort` is a recognised field. Under `--strict-config` it is accepted and the turn completes, while a deliberately misspelled `model_reasoning_effrot` is REFUSED with "unknown configuration field". The control is what makes the acceptance mean something.
  - **Allowed safe passthrough**: the resume option surface is enumerated in the record. The load-bearing half is what `exec` has and `resume` does NOT: `--sandbox`, `--cd`, `--add-dir`, `--approve-for-me`, `--color`, `--local-provider`, `--oss`, `--profile`, `--version`.

YOUR WORK, and it is bounded.

  (1) **Complete 11.1's qualification and land the matching adapter assertions.** The `work-site` entry already reads `supported` under the 2026-09-15 operator ruling and both identity fields already name 0.154.0 — that is not yours to change. What is yours is the assertions 11.1 asks for, as tests over the argv the adapter composes and the decisions the gate makes:
      - a resume argv carries the class through `-c sandbox_mode=<class>` and NEVER through `-s`;
      - the stdin prompt positional and the effort field are composed as the measured interface allows;
      - an option absent from the resume surface never travels to a resume;
      - identity, boundary, hands or accounting mismatch still refuses with its proper token, and absence of markers still declines.
    Prove each by removal: break the line it claims, watch it fail, restore, and say so with the exact test and assertion.

  (2) **Tick 11.1 only if its WHOLE acceptance is evidenced.** If any part is not, leave it unticked and say precisely what is missing. Preserving the shipping disposition does not complete an enablement task, and the task text says so itself.

WHAT IS NOT YOURS, and this fence is the point of the commission. Tasks 10.6, 10.7 and 10.8 are Claude, DSH and LaneTally proofs — each needs a live provider measurement that only the controller can take, and none is taken. Their enablement tasks 11.2, 11.3 and 11.4 stay unticked. Tasks 8.8, 8.10 and 9.6 depend on passes C and D, which have never been commissioned. Groups 14 and 15 are re-pins and pre-archive gates that cannot start until groups 8 through 14 complete. Do not tick, start, or plan any of them.

Two shapes are NEW in 0.154.0 and were never previously supported — `--worktree` (a managed git worktree session) and `--thread-source`. A preservation proof does not qualify them. If the adapter can compose them at all, prove they are REFUSED on a resume, the way the last slice proved it by adding each to the allow-list and watching the test fail.

DO NOT TRADE SAFETY FOR THE RULING. The operator ruled that the rejoin main performs today stays live. That is not licence to enable a shape whose confinement is unknown: absence of markers still declines, and every refusal token the gate emits today still emits.

STATE OF THE BRANCH, and keep it true. Cut from main at 9da5ff92. The exact coverage gate demands literal equality on lines, branches and functions, so every line you add is a line it will demand covered. fmt, clippy across all targets and features, the crate suites, both bundle compiles and strict OpenSpec validation must all pass.

HOW TO MEASURE COVERAGE. Use a writable disk-backed TMPDIR OUTSIDE the repository; an in-repo TMPDIR breaks the ledger tests and the box's global TMPDIR may be read-only from a seat. Boundary tests skip inside the box, which cannot create a bwrap namespace on this host, so in-box equality is unattainable and is not your failure (#286). Report your in-box numbers; the host measurement is the controller's.

THREE HOUSE LESSONS FROM THIS WEEK, each of which cost CI rounds. Stage any file you are about to execute beside its target and `rename` it into place; never write at the target path (#255). Never assert a refusal as `is_err()` alone — assert the REASON, because a call that failed for an unrelated cause satisfies `is_err()` while the check under test is never reached. And a fixture whose text is one or two characters makes a `contains` assertion vacuous: it will match a temp path on some platform and pass everywhere else.

IF YOU RUN OUT OF ROOM. Return `oversized`, never `broken`. Item (1) is the substance; item (2) is the honest accounting of it. Partial progress is adopted by the next visit.

KNOWN ENVIRONMENT DEFECTS — do not rediscover them. #282: the installed DSH core forwards GIT_CONFIG_COUNT but filters GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0, so prefix any git call, git init in tests included, with `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`. #281: a DeepSeek seat records no turns and no tokens; a harness defect.

PROVIDER INSTRUCTION, operator-set for this run. Codex (gpt-6-astra at xhigh) JUDGES: triage, clarify, the chief architect, analyze and the review chief, plus every review position. Claude DELIVERS: implement, the SDD smith and the task planner. A judge and the hand it judges are deliberately different providers here.

REVIEW POSITIONS state findings and evidence. They do not direct a verdict, do not tell a gate where to send the work, and do not claim another office's power.

CONSTRAINTS. Commit completed work unsigned. Never push, merge, or start another Brokkr run from a seat; the controller owns remote CI, publication, integration and closure.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including all three operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Five platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew, Scoop and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```
